Measured positive. The Committee notes strong job gains and a low unemployment rate, expects inflation to move toward 2 percent, and raised the federal funds rate while keeping policy accommodative. In New Keynesian models with Calvo-style price stickiness, inflation adjusts gradually via the Phillips curve inflation-adjustment equation, so a forecast of inflation drifting to target as slack diminishes is consistent with theory. The rise in market-based inflation compensation, though still low, suggests expectations remain anchored near target; inflation-forecast targeting frameworks (e.g., Svensson; Svensson and Woodford) emphasize that credible targets stabilize expectations, allowing gradualism. The gradual path for a funds rate still below the long-run level aligns with Taylor-type/estimated policy rules (Rudebusch) and supports stability under learning (Evans and Honkapohja), reducing risks of price-level indeterminacy. Given these literature-backed considerations—strong labor conditions and credible price-stability objectives balanced against still-below-target inflation and moderated spending/investment—the tone is cautiously optimistic.
